scope: 30 selected primary sources; method coverage, not an exhaustive survey; no third-party code copied and no inference calls made
status_policy: paper results are author-reported; official competition placements are identified separately; no current Terminal-Bench 4.0 numerical rank verified

sources.title: PAL: Program-aided Language Models
sources.verified_point: Language model generates program steps; execution is delegated to an interpreter.
sources.our_use: Compute table joins, optimization and arithmetic through Python, then validate interpretation.

sources.title: Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents
sources.verified_point: CodeAct uses executable Python as a unified action space and revises actions from interpreter feedback.
sources.our_use: Small executable actions, bounded output and targeted recovery.
sources.caution: Paper evaluation uses different models and benchmarks; no transferred numerical promise.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
sources.verified_point: Interleaves reasoning, environment actions and observations.
sources.our_use: Readable baseline control loop; useful observations rather than extra agent roles.

sources.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
sources.verified_point: Investigates repository navigation, editing and test interfaces for software agents.
sources.our_use: Clear bounded read/edit/run tools and informative error messages.

sources.title: mini-SWE-agent
sources.version: main identifies v2; viewed 2026-11-08; commit SHA unavailable through accessible viewer
sources.verified_point: Small agent class, bash actions, linear history and independent subprocess execution.
sources.our_use: Prefer a short understandable loop to layered orchestration.
sources.caution: README benchmark score is not used as a verified current leaderboard placement.

sources.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
sources.verified_point: Localization, small diff candidates and regression/reproduction-test selection; generated reproduction tests can be incorrect.
sources.our_use: One localized candidate, independently justified checks, at most a bounded repair attempt.
sources.caution: Full method samples many candidates and tests; do not assume its cost or score transfers.

sources.title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
sources.verified_point: Platform integrates code, shell and environment interaction with evaluation support.
sources.our_use: Borrow execution principles, keep mandatory openJiuwen and small deployment.
sources.code_license: MIT for checked root license; components need separate inspection before copying

sources.title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
sources.verified_point: EvalPlus expands tests using generated and mutated inputs and exposes missed errors and ranking changes.
sources.our_use: Separate visible examples from stronger hidden checks across edge cases.

sources.title: CoverUp: Effective High Coverage Test Generation for Python
sources.version: v4, 2025-05-09; title changed from earlier versions
sources.verified_point: Combines line/branch coverage, source context and execution feedback for Python test generation.
sources.our_use: Target untested branches during development, do not equate coverage with correct behavior.

sources.title: Design choices made by LLM-based test generators prevent them from finding bugs
sources.verified_point: Passing-oracle design can validate buggy behavior or reject bug-revealing tests.
sources.our_use: Derive expected behavior from specification or independent computation.

sources.title: Metamorphic Testing: A New Approach for Generating Next Test Cases
sources.verified_point: Generate follow-up cases and check required relations between executions.
sources.our_use: Condition-dependent invariants such as permutation or consistent renaming.
sources.caution: A proposed invariant must hold for the actual specification.

sources.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
sources.verified_point: Single model iteratively generates, critiques and refines without parameter updates.
sources.our_use: Optional bounded correction, preferably grounded in execution failure.
sources.caution: Additional feedback calls consume budget and can repeat the same misconception.

sources.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
sources.verified_point: Keeps linguistic feedback from failed trials in episodic memory rather than updating weights.
sources.our_use: A short failure hypothesis with the next correction attempt.
sources.caution: A reflection without reliable feedback is not evidence of improvement.

sources.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning Acting and Planning in Language Models
sources.verified_point: Combines tree search, model evaluation/reflection and environment feedback.
sources.our_use: Consider bounded alternative candidates only after measuring a reliable selector.
sources.caution: Search increases cost; original HumanEval results do not establish contest performance.

sources.title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
sources.verified_point: Compares masking and summarization; main masking window is ten turns; effectiveness depends on trajectory length and scaffold.
sources.our_use: Compare full history with small windows, keeping task and essential errors available.
sources.caution: Windows of two or four turns are our proposed ablation, not the authors' best setting.

sources.title: SWE-Pruner: Self-Adaptive Context Pruning for Coding Agents
sources.verified_point: Goal-conditioned context pruning uses a trained 0.6B neural skimmer.
sources.our_use: Motivates selective source reading; use ordinary search instead under no-local-neural-network restriction.
sources.caution: Ready-made neural skimmer is not admissible under our stated runtime limits.

sources.title: Recursive Language Models
sources.verified_point: Treats long inputs as external environment data, inspected by programs and recursive model calls.
sources.our_use: Keep large files outside prompt and read relevant slices; recursion is optional and separately budgeted.
sources.caution: Long-context results do not prove benefit for our short tasks.

sources.title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
sources.verified_point: Discusses prompt adaptation, approximation and learned model cascades.
sources.our_use: Evaluate a cheap attempt followed by escalation after a checkable failure.
sources.caution: Published monetary savings do not transfer to our weighted-token budget and fixed Qwen menu.

sources.title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs with Preference Data
sources.verified_point: Learns routing between stronger and weaker models from preference data.
sources.our_use: First measure the four allowed models; start with transparent rules instead of a local neural router.
sources.caution: Single-turn routing evidence is not evidence of whole-agent optimality.

sources.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution
sources.verified_point: Composable segment-cost forecasts update from prefixes without extra model calls. Budget study is offline trace-completion replay, not task-resolution evaluation.
sources.our_use: Passive forecast first, then live equal-budget policy comparison.
sources.caution: Reported 21.3 percent replay savings must not be described as solved-task improvement.

sources.title: TokenCast official implementation
sources.version: main viewed 2026-11-08; two commits shown; commit SHA unavailable through accessible viewer
sources.verified_point: Current tree includes src, configs, tests, examples and a local LightGBM runtime; no longer README-only.
sources.our_use: Inspect algorithm and compare independently; no implementation copied.

sources.title: AgentX–AgentBeats competition, Phase 2 winners
sources.verified_point: Organizer lists AgentWhetters first for SWE-bench Pro and publishes team descriptions, including simple loop, test gate and final diff collection.
sources.our_use: Completion gate and final artifact preservation; deterministic output shaping.
sources.caution: Placements are competition-specific; engineering descriptions are team accounts, not our replication.
sources.code_license: not applicable to organizer page; implementation assessed separately

sources.title: AgentWhetters SWE-bench Pro Purple Agent, simple loop
sources.version: main viewed 2026-11-08; 23 commits shown; commit SHA unavailable through accessible viewer
sources.verified_point: Probes original tests, rejects done on new regressions, allows a bounded QA phase and collects diff after step exhaustion.
sources.our_use: Independent implementation of completion validation and checkpoint behavior.
sources.caution: Uses GPT-5.4 high effort and a different evaluator; no automatic Qwen transfer.
sources.code_license: no explicit license found in accessible root listing; no code reused

sources.title: Terminal-Bench 4.0 official release explanation
sources.verified_point: Changes environment resources, removes tasks and fixes others; requires rerunning trials across breaking version changes.
sources.our_use: Freeze benchmark version and resources for meaningful comparisons.
sources.caution: Its eight-hour per-task timeout differs substantially from our total one-hour limit.

sources.title: Terminal-Bench official current leaderboard surface
sources.verified_point: Page labels Terminal-Bench 4.0 and score/cost/token columns.
sources.our_use: Keep current leaderboard separate from historical engineering writeups.
sources.caution: Numerical rows not exposed in text retrieval; no current first place, ranking or percentage verified.

sources.title: Terminal-Bench Leaderboard Integrity Update
sources.verified_point: Requires passing trajectories and distinguishes reward hacking from cheating, with invalidation policies.
sources.our_use: Preserve evidence; test intended behavior rather than exploit evaluator artifacts.
sources.caution: These are Terminal-Bench rules; our hackathon regulations remain the governing contract.

sources.title: Terminal-RSI: Recursive Self-Improving Terminal Agents via Recursive Self-Rewrite and Policy-Refine
sources.verified_point: Alternates verified trajectory rewriting and policy refinement from a Qwen3.8-27B base; method changes model parameters.
sources.our_use: Failure taxonomy and strict terminal verification, not checkpoint substitution.
sources.caution: Reported benchmark scores are paper claims; trained derivative is outside our fixed allowed-model setup.

sources.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
sources.verified_point: Proposes reusable agent-native primitives composed and revised with environment verification.
sources.our_use: Small reusable operations tied to observed failures, rather than whole framework adoption.
sources.caution: Fresh author-reported results; resident model/service machinery is not automatically compatible with our restrictions.

sources.title: How Do AI Agents Waste Your Money?
sources.verified_point: Validates identified token waste by deleting spans and resuming execution to assess outcome changes.
sources.our_use: Intervention-based comparison of history policies, beyond aggregate token counts.
sources.caution: Fresh paper; extra model judging has its own cost and is not included in our proposed first version.

sources.title: Warp: How we scored number one on Terminal-Bench (52 percent), historical engineering writeup
sources.verified_point: Describes model-chain experiments, controlling long-running commands and maintained plans.
sources.our_use: Bounded command execution and small task-state reminders; measure planning overhead.
sources.caution: Organizer news confirms historical first place on 2025-06-25, not current Terminal-Bench 4.0 leadership.
